headline: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after breach exposed customer Kubernetes clusters and secrets

headline: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore uses IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor against Cyprus telecoms and infrastructure
summary: Researchers describe Volant Manticore, an Iran-aligned espionage group not previously documented. It has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. Its KuboShell backdoor uses IPFS for command and control and deploys a post-compromise framework called Homa.

summary: watchTowr reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-120705 (arbitrary file read, CVSS 8.6) and CVE-2026-129243 in GeoServer. headline: FBI declines to give details of National Crime Information Center breach, citing investigation
summary: The FBI's National Crime Information Center database has reportedly been breached. This is the bureau's second breach in recent months. FBI Director Kash Patel declined to give details, citing the ongoing investigation.

headline: US Treasury FinCEN investigates cyber incident amid reports of other federal agency breaches
summary: The Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network is investigating a cyber incident and has taken some services offline. The report puts the incident alongside other reported breaches at federal agencies. Few details have been released so far.

headline: US Treasury's FinCEN takes some systems offline after unauthorized access
summary: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) reported a cyber incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems and took some services offline as a precaution. FinCEN collects suspicious activity reports and other Bank Secrecy Act filings from financial institutions. Reports of other federal agency breaches surfaced at the same time, and the scope of the incident has not yet been determined.

headline: Attacker exploits CVSS 10.0 RCE flaw to run commands on six Hex.pm registry servers
summary: An attacker ran operating system commands on six production servers of Hex.pm, the package registry for Elixir and Erlang. The flaw had been in the registry's code since 2016. Maintainers had all servers on a patched build within about 15 minutes of the first malicious request, and integrity checks are reported to be under way.

headline: AP source: unclassified CIA system breached in cyberattack
summary: According to an AP source, an unclassified CIA system was breached in a cyberattack. It is not yet clear what information was compromised or who carried out the attack.

headline: Cyberattack takes down Colorado's myColorado app; data of about 150,000 users likely stolen
summary: Colorado says a cyberattack took its myColorado state services app offline. Officials believe data on about 150,000 users was likely stolen. Residents use the app for digital ID, document storage and access to state services.

headline: Hackers breach unclassified US intelligence OSINT system used by CIA and ODNI
summary: Hackers compromised an unclassified intelligence system that serves the CIA and ODNI, which CyberScoop reports appears related to open-source intelligence. A source said no other systems are currently at risk. Who is responsible and what data was affected have not been disclosed.

summary: Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the US CIA. Details on the method and scope are not confirmed in the available summary.

summary: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is investigating a cybersecurity incident and has taken systems offline. Its filing portal is still working, and deadlines for affected filers have been extended. The cause and scope have not been disclosed.

summary: Cyberattacks are increasingly hitting industrial systems in Latin America. Reported examples include the Port of Santos in Brazil and a pipeline in Argentina.

headline: Study: bots abuse AWS keys leaked in public Docker images within seconds
summary: Stony Brook University researchers planted 300 decoy Docker images on public registries. Bots found and used a leaked AWS access key in under eight seconds, showing how quickly secrets in published container images are exploited.

headline: US lawmakers urge identity verification firms to strengthen security after IDscan breach
summary: A bipartisan letter from members of both chambers of Congress warns that identity verification companies still have significant security gaps. The letter follows IDscan's data breach in September.

headline: Researchers find 'God Mode' flaws in visa and immigration systems of six countries
summary: Researchers found several flaws in the online visa and immigration systems of Nigeria, Ethiopia, Zambia, Sri Lanka, Fiji and Ghana. The flaws could have let attackers disrupt traveler entry. The source does not report any exploitation.

headline: VulnCheck data shows credential harvesting rising sharply as a goal of vulnerability exploitation
summary: VulnCheck canary data for January to November 2026 shows that credential theft made up 13% of recorded exploitation activity. Its monthly share rose to between 25% and 35% by September and October. Of 694 exploited CVEs, 127 were used at least once to steal database passwords, cloud keys, API tokens or SSH keys.

headline: Anthropic opens public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards for zero-data-retention customers
summary: Anthropic has opened a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards. The feature analyses conversations stored in customer-controlled cloud environments to flag potentially harmful AI activity while keeping zero data retention. Security teams receive the flags and investigate them.

headline: OpenSSL QUIC stream reassembly flaw allows memory exhaustion in non-default setups (CVE-2026-84785)
summary: A remote peer can send many small out-of-order QUIC stream fragments to make OpenSSL keep a large number of reassembly nodes in memory, which can lead to denial of service. Only applications that accept incoming peer-initiated streams are exposed; the default policy rejects them. Memory use is limited by flow control, and the affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

headline: Zstandard 1.5.1–1.5.7 flaw can leak internal buffer contents through decompression output
summary: CVE-2026-124851 affects Zstandard 1.5.1 through 1.5.7. Specially crafted compressed data can expose a 64 KiB internal buffer, which may contain uninitialized memory or data from earlier decompressions. The attacker must be able to submit compressed data and see the output. No exploitation is reported, and the record does not confirm Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

headline: Valkey cluster-mode heap overflow lets authenticated users crash the server, possibly enabling RCE (CVE-2026-136156)

Fixes are in 7.2.15, 8.0.12, 8.1.11, 9.0.7 and 9.1.3, and no exploitation has been reported.

summary: CVE-2026-135610 is an invalid-pointer flaw in the Audio/Video: Playback component. It is fixed in Firefox ESR 153.8 and Thunderbird 153.8. The source reports no severity or exploitation details.

headline: Thunderbird CardDAV flaw could leak address book credentials to authenticating HTTP proxies
summary: CVE-2026-136230 lets Thunderbird answer an HTTP proxy's authentication request with the CardDAV server's username and password. This can happen during setup and during background sync, even over HTTPS. Thunderbird 161 and 153.8 fix it. The Amazon Linux record does not show whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched.

headline: Use-after-free in Firefox DOM Core & HTML component fixed, including ESR 115
summary: CVE-2026-135518 is a use-after-free flaw in the DOM: Core & HTML component. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46 and 153.8, and Thunderbird 161 and 153.8. No exploitation has been reported, and the Amazon Linux record does not show whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Use-after-free in Firefox and Thunderbird Cache API storage component fixed
summary: CVE-2026-135590 is a use-after-free flaw in the Storage: Cache API component. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. No exploitation has been reported, and the Amazon Linux record does not show whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Use-after-free in Firefox and Thunderbird DOM Workers component fixed
summary: CVE-2026-135570 is a use-after-free flaw in the DOM: Workers component. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. No exploitation has been reported, and the Amazon Linux record does not show whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: China-aligned Webworm group uses custom-built SoftEther VPN to evade detection
summary: Researchers report that the Webworm espionage group, which is aligned with China, rebuilt SoftEther VPN from its source code. The group stripped out artifacts that defenders normally use to spot the tool, so it can keep covert access to networks.

headline: Eclypsium report: exploited network appliance flaws mostly in bundled third-party components
summary: Eclypsium's November InfraTrust report finds that most recent advisories for exploited infrastructure vulnerabilities involved bundled third-party software rather than vendor-written code. This highlights supply-chain risk in network appliances. The summary does not name specific products.

headline: FFmpeg RTP RFC4175 handler leaks heap memory into decoded video frames
summary: CVE-2026-135727 affects FFmpeg versions before 9.1. Crafted RTP streams that carry only part of a frame can leave buffer bytes uninitialized, so heap memory from the process leaks into displayed, stored or re-streamed video. The source does not confirm Amazon Linux status.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird 161 fix boundary condition flaw in JavaScript engine (CVE-2026-135574)
summary: Mozilla fixed incorrect boundary conditions in the JavaScript Engine component in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched. No severity or exploitation details are given.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix boundary condition flaw in Networking Cache, including ESR 115 (CVE-2026-135515)
summary: Mozilla fixed incorrect boundary conditions in the Networking: Cache component. Fixed versions are Firefox 161, ESR 115.46, ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. The Amazon Linux record does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix frame poisoning flaw in DOM Core & HTML (CVE-2026-135609)
summary: Mozilla fixed a frame poisoning flaw in the DOM: Core & HTML component in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. The Amazon Linux record does not say whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available. No severity score or exploitation is reported.

headline: Microsoft adds a Visio RCE CVE that was fixed in November 2026 but left out of the release notes
summary: Microsoft has published CVE-2026-112732, a remote code execution flaw in Office Visio. The November 2026 security updates already fixed it, but the CVE was left out of that month's release notes. Microsoft says this is an informational change only, and systems with the November updates need no further action.

headline: Vendor research finds most leaked secrets remain valid for years because revoking them is slow
summary: GitGuardian's State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 found that more than 64% of valid secrets discovered in 2022 still worked in January 2026. Teams delay revoking them because they cannot tell what a revocation will break. The vendor argues that triaging by validity alone misses many critical secrets and recommends prioritizing by what each credential can access and whether it was exposed publicly.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix invalid pointer flaw in DOM Networking component (CVE-2026-135503)
summary: An invalid pointer issue in the DOM: Networking component is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46 and 153.8, and Thunderbird 161 and 153.8. The source does not give its impact or say whether it has been exploited.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix mitigation bypass in DOM Security component (CVE-2026-135573)
summary: A flaw in the DOM: Security component could let an attacker bypass a security mitigation. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, and Thunderbird 161 and 153.8. No exploitation or severity score is reported.

headline: Thunderbird OpenPGP sender spoofing via duplicate From header (CVE-2026-136226)
summary: A lowercase From header placed before the real one can make Thunderbird display a different sender than the one whose OpenPGP signature was verified. Anyone whose key the victim has accepted could send messages that appear validly signed by another sender. The issue is fixed in Thunderbird 161 and 153.8.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix information disclosure flaw in DOM File component (CVE-2026-135572)
summary: Mozilla fixed an information disclosure flaw in the DOM: File component in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. The sources give no severity score and no reports of exploitation. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird fix invalid pointer flaw in DOM Navigation component (CVE-2026-135544)
summary: Mozilla fixed an invalid pointer flaw in the DOM: Navigation component in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 115.46, Firefox ESR 153.8 and the matching Thunderbird releases. This kind of memory-safety bug could be exploitable, but the sources report no exploitation and give no severity score. Amazon Linux status is not established.

headline: Dutch experts question legality of employer biometric face scans
summary: Experts in the Netherlands have criticized biometric face scans used by companies including DHL, YoungCapital and Randstad, with some calling the practice illegal. The source summary does not say whether any regulator has acted.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird 161 fix address bar spoofing issue (CVE-2026-135559)
summary: Mozilla fixed a spoofing issue in the Address Bar component in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. Address bar spoofing could help phishing pages look legitimate, though no exploitation is reported. The Amazon Linux record does not establish whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: Wireshark RTP RFC2198 dissector type confusion causes heap memory corruption (CVE-2026-130448)
summary: A crafted capture with Exported PDU metadata can pass TCP metadata to Wireshark's RTP RFC2198 dissector without a type check, leading to a heap out-of-bounds read and write. Opening the file crashes Wireshark, and TShark crashes when run with -V. The source does not establish exploitation or Amazon Linux status.

headline: Thunderbird flaws let attackers replay old signed emails that still show a valid signature
summary: Two Thunderbird flaws (CVE-2026-136228 and CVE-2026-136229) let an attacker resend an old signed message so it shows as validly signed again. They work through missing or unparseable Date headers, multiple Date headers in S/MIME, or OpenPGP messages that are both signed and encrypted. Both get around the protection added for CVE-2022-2226 and are fixed in Thunderbird 161 and 153.8.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird 161 fix unspecified issue in Audio/Video GMP component (CVE-2026-135602)
summary: Mozilla fixed an unspecified issue in the Audio/Video: GMP component in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched. No severity or exploitation details are given.

headline: Use-after-free in Firefox and Thunderbird DOM fixed across current and ESR branches (CVE-2026-135553)
summary: Mozilla fixed a use-after-free in the DOM: Core & HTML component. The fix is in Firefox 161, ESR 115.46, ESR 153.8 and the matching Thunderbird releases. Memory-safety flaws of this type can sometimes lead to code execution, but the source states no severity and reports no exploitation.

headline: Amazon Linux lists CVE-2026-135901 security fix for shadow newgidmap
summary: Amazon Linux Security Center published a CVE record for a security fix to newgidmap in the shadow package. The record does not establish which Amazon Linux versions are affected or whether patches are available, and no severity or exploitation details are provided.

headline: Thunderbird attachment flaw could leak local files when user forwards a crafted attachment
summary: CVE-2026-136231 lets a received message carry an attachment that points to an arbitrary local file under a misleading name. If a user drags that attachment into a new message and sends it, the local file's contents go out with the message. The flaw is fixed in Thunderbird 161 and 153.8. The Amazon Linux record does not show whether Amazon Linux is affected.

headline: ShinyHunters claims return as Okta notes possible links to new Inception group
summary: An account associated with ShinyHunters has announced that the group is back. Okta reports possible connections between the newly observed Inception group and ShinyHunters actors, which Inception denies. The details of the alleged links are not confirmed.

headline: Boundary-condition flaw in Skia graphics in Firefox and Thunderbird fixed (CVE-2026-135535)
summary: Mozilla fixed incorrect boundary conditions in the Graphics: Skia component. The fix is in Firefox 161, ESR 115.46, ESR 153.8 and the matching Thunderbird releases. The source states no severity and reports no exploitation.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird 161 fix side-channel flaw in Networking: HTTP component (CVE-2026-135586)
summary: Mozilla fixed a side-channel weakness in the Networking: HTTP component in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. The source gives no severity score and reports no exploitation. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux packages are affected or patched.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird Cycle Collector use-after-free fixed in version 161
summary: CVE-2026-135575 is a use-after-free in the Cycle Collector component. It is fixed in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. The record gives no exploitation status or severity score.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird DOM Security information disclosure fixed in 161 and ESR 153.8
summary: CVE-2026-135587 is an information-disclosure flaw in the DOM: Security component. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. No exploitation is reported.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird WebGPU invalid-pointer flaw fixed in 161 and ESR 153.8
summary: CVE-2026-135516 is an invalid-pointer bug in the Graphics: WebGPU component. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. Memory-safety bugs like this can sometimes allow code execution, but the record does not state the impact, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: Frame-poisoning flaw in Firefox and Thunderbird layout engine fixed (CVE-2026-135608)
summary: Mozilla fixed a frame-poisoning issue in the Layout component in Firefox 161, ESR 153.8 and the matching Thunderbird releases. The source states no severity and reports no exploitation.

headline: Race condition in Firefox and Thunderbird Networking: HTTP fixed in 161 and ESR 153.8 (CVE-2026-135528)
summary: Mozilla fixed a race condition in the Networking: HTTP component in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8 and the matching Thunderbird releases. The source gives no severity score and reports no exploitation. Amazon Linux affected status has not been established.

headline: Talos analyzes tradecraft of OpenAI-linked agentic attack swarm
summary: Cisco Talos examined tradecraft from an OpenAI-linked agentic swarm active in 2026, which it says can be traced through public records. The analysis compares that activity with early signs of agentic attacks seen in the wild.

headline: Firefox and Thunderbird 161 fix boundary condition flaw in Widget: Gtk component (CVE-2026-135591)
summary: An incorrect boundary condition in the Widget: Gtk component, which is used on Linux builds, is fixed in Firefox 161 and Thunderbird 161. The source does not give its impact or say whether it has been exploited.

headline: DIVD publishes forensic report on hack, citing ARP spoofing by attacker
summary: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) has published a forensic investigation report on a hack. The report says the attacker carried out an ARP spoofing attack. The source summary does not name the affected organisation or describe the impact.

headline: ShinyHunters claims return on new leak site after FBI arrests, citing old PGP keys as proof
summary: The ShinyHunters extortion group claims to have returned through a new data leak site, following two months of arrests of alleged members. It cites old PGP keys as proof of identity. The claim has not been independently verified.

headline: Carnegie Endowment donor data exposed in breach at vendor Soapbox Engage
summary: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace says some donor information was leaked. The leak came from a cyberattack on its third-party vendor, Soapbox Engage. The source does not give the scope of the exposure.

headline: NCC Group reports 23% rise in ransomware attacks in October after a record quarter
summary: NCC Group researchers report that ransomware attacks rose 23% in October, following a record quarter. They suggest the continued increase may reflect a new threat environment.

headline: Flatpak portal flaw CVE-2026-133845 could expose file descriptors to a subsandbox
summary: An unprivileged Flatpak app could trick flatpak-portal into giving a subsandbox access to one of the app's own file descriptors. The CVE record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available. No exploitation is reported.

headline: Flatpak system-helper privilege escalation flaw CVE-2026-133842 disclosed
summary: The flatpak-system-helper extra-data handling could allow privilege escalation when canonicalizing permissions fails with an EMFILE error, meaning the process has run out of file descriptors. The CVE record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched. No exploitation is reported.

headline: WordPress removes six backdoored WP Connect plugins after suspected developer account compromise
summary: WordPress removed six plugins from developer WP Connect after backdoored versions enabling arbitrary code execution were pushed on November 22, 2026. The developer's account was likely compromised. The WordPress plugins team says it detected and blocked the malicious releases before they were officially published, which suggests sites saw limited exposure.

headline: CVE-2026-44842 addresses parser resource exhaustion through unlimited nesting depth
summary: The CVE record describes a parser fix that limits nesting depth by default, because deep nesting grows stack use and processing work. The record does not name the affected component or confirm Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

headline: Suspected ransomware attack disrupts care at Guadeloupe University Hospital
summary: France's national cybersecurity agency is investigating a suspected ransomware attack on the University Hospital of Guadeloupe. Surgeries have been postponed, some cancer treatments suspended, and staff have gone back to paper. No group has been named.

headline: Turnitin discloses unauthorized activity on customer-facing systems
summary: Turnitin's CEO said the company detected unauthorized activity involving some customer-facing systems. The source does not give details on scope, data exposure or the attacker.

headline: Turnitin investigates cyberattack, says its systems remain operational
summary: The edtech company Turnitin, which makes a plagiarism checker, is investigating a cyberattack. The company says its systems are fully operational and safe to use. It has not disclosed details about the attack or any data exposure.

headline: Unspecified Internationalization issue fixed in Firefox and Thunderbird
summary: CVE-2026-135603 is an unspecified issue in the Internationalization component of Firefox and Thunderbird. It is fixed in Firefox 161, Firefox ESR 153.8, Thunderbird 161 and Thunderbird 153.8. Its impact is not described and no exploitation has been reported.

headline: FFmpeg NIST SPHERE parser flaw can leak uninitialized memory (CVE-2026-135707)
summary: FFmpeg versions before 9.1 contain an inverted allocation check in the NIST SPHERE demuxer. A crafted file can leak an uninitialized heap byte or, if allocation fails, cause a NULL pointer write. No exploitation has been reported.

headline: Socket releases free patches for critical CVEs in RubyGems dependencies
summary: Socket has released free security patches that it says cover all critical CVEs in RubyGems packages. The patches let teams fix those vulnerabilities without upgrading dependencies. This is a vendor product announcement.

headline: Dutch DPA says municipalities should inform threatened residents about postal address option
summary: The Dutch data protection authority (AP) says municipalities should tell residents who face threats that they can register a postal address instead of their home address. The guidance deals with protecting personal data held in Dutch municipal records.

headline: FFmpeg DXA demuxer flaw can leak uninitialised memory (CVE-2026-135719)
summary: FFmpeg versions before 9.1 do not handle short reads of DXA palette data, so uninitialised stack bytes can end up in decoded frames. Exploiting it requires a crafted stream delivered over a stalling network source. The impact is information disclosure, and no exploitation is reported.

headline: Researcher launches tracker of AI-assisted hacking incidents and offensive tools
summary: Daniel Miessler has started tracking reported incidents of AI-enhanced hacking and the offensive AI tooling ("harnesses") the attackers use. Bruce Schneier highlighted the effort on his blog. The source does not describe any specific new incident.

headline: University uses DSPM to discover sensitive data and tighten access ahead of AI adoption
summary: Southeastern University used data security posture management to locate sensitive information and tighten access controls. The work is described as groundwork for safer AI adoption. This is a vendor-style case study, not a security incident.

headline: Legal Q&A: when to send customers follow-up updates after a data breach
summary: This reader legal question asks when an organization has to re-notify customers with updates after a data breach that was already reported to the Dutch DPA. It covers GDPR breach-communication duties.

headline: OpenAI and Cisco launch a framework that lets AI agents temporarily block vulnerability exploitation
summary: OpenAI and Cisco have released a framework that lets AI agents apply temporary protections against vulnerability exploitation. It is meant to cover systems while organizations test patches, and the source URL suggests it targets Linux. This is a product launch, not a threat.

headline: Ground infrastructure weaknesses raise satellite service cyber risk
summary: A Dark Reading analysis argues that the ground infrastructure behind satellite services is a growing weak point as space activity expands. The piece is a commentary on risk, not a report of a specific incident.

headline: Unit 42 outlines defensive strategies against AI-driven cyberattacks
summary: Unit 42 looks at how AI-enabled attacks are evolving. It recommends speed, edge AI and behavioural baselines as defences.

headline: McAfee survey: share of Americans reporting holiday shopping scams nearly doubled
summary: McAfee research says 42% of Americans report falling for a holiday shopping scam, up from 22% in 2025. Fewer shoppers now feel confident they can spot online scams.

headline: California Privacy Protection Agency director Kemp to step down
summary: The director of the California Privacy Protection Agency is leaving after two years. His departure follows the launch of a platform that lets consumers opt out of data sharing.

headline: Cyber insurers describe a growing divide between organisations with and without AI defences
summary: In a podcast episode, cyber insurers discuss how AI is changing the threat landscape. They argue that pressure on both insurers and policyholders is making the current insurance model unsustainable.

headline: Former OpenAI employee accused of planting recording device granted $1M bail
summary: A San Francisco federal judge granted bail of $1 million to a former OpenAI employee. The employee is accused of hiding a covert recording device in the company's offices. He was arrested in October 2026.

headline: Shufti launches Fraud Hub to link identity, device and behavioural fraud signals
summary: Shufti has launched Fraud Hub, a product that correlates identity, device, biometric and behavioural signals. It is designed to detect coordinated fraud networks across the user lifecycle.

headline: UK government considers extending mandatory age verification to eBay, Vinted and other sites
summary: The UK government is considering extending the mandatory age verification that applies to social media to marketplaces such as eBay and Vinted. This is still at the consideration stage and no decision has been made.

headline: Firefox for Android WebExtensions spoofing flaw fixed in Firefox 161
summary: CVE-2026-135594 is a spoofing issue in the WebExtensions component of Firefox for Android. Firefox 161 fixes it. The record gives no severity score and no exploitation reports.

headline: Developer essay identifies three inflection points in LLM coding-agent capability over the past year
summary: Simon Willison reflects on a year of progress in LLM coding agents, from Claude Opus 4.5 to the "Fable class" models. He also notes that a model with strong cybersecurity capabilities was withheld and that export controls were applied. This is an opinion piece with no security incident.

headline: Vendor article: AI may reduce reporting workload for penetration testers
summary: PentestPad describes how AI can take over documentation and reporting work in penetration tests. It says this can be done while keeping client data on the testing team's own infrastructure.

headline: University CISO interview on building a security program on a limited budget
summary: SecurityWeek interviews Matthew Martin, Chief Information Security and Privacy Officer at Western Carolina University. He discusses how to build a security program without an enterprise-level budget.

headline: Belgian police advise disabling default admin accounts on smart devices
summary: Belgian police are advising consumers to disable the default admin user on smart devices. They recommend using a separate account with a different name instead.

headline: CVE-2026-129820: ConfigHash accepts invalid keys, producing malformed saved output
summary: A CVE record says a ConfigHash component accepts invalid keys, which leads to malformed output when the configuration is saved. The source does not name the affected product, impact or Amazon Linux status.

headline: Europol-coordinated operation disrupts 57 illegal IPTV services and traces €26 million in crypto
summary: Police from 11 countries, coordinated by Europol, disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and identified 321 pirate websites. Investigators traced more than €26 million in cryptocurrency. No arrests have been announced so far, and analysis of the transactions is still ongoing.

headline: Microsoft resolves Microsoft 365 issue that blocked access to Office apps
summary: Microsoft has fixed a known issue that stopped some Microsoft 365 customers from using Office applications. This was a reliability problem, not a security incident.

headline: CVE-2026-129821: ConfigHash accepts invalid keys, causing malformed saved output
summary: A CVE record says a ConfigHash function accepts invalid keys, which leads to malformed output when the configuration is saved. The record does not name the affected product or describe any security impact. Amazon Linux status is not established.

headline: gputaskman released as open-source terminal GPU task manager
summary: gputaskman is a new open-source terminal tool that shows which processes are using GPU memory and compute. Where it finds evidence, it also tries to identify the AI model behind each process.

headline: Historian reports GPT-6.2 Astra identified the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook
summary: A history professor says GPT-6.2 Astra used public sources to identify the probable creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook in about 22 minutes. The piece looks at how agentic AI could affect historical research. It has no security implications.

headline: SANS ISC Stormcast daily podcast for 23 November 2026
summary: SANS ISC has published its daily Stormcast podcast episode. The source gives no details about which topics it covers.

headline: Talos profile: Pierre Cadieux on his path from help desk to security
summary: This is a Cisco Talos staff profile. Pierre Cadieux describes his early help-desk work and how correlating Windows and Unix logs led him into security.

headline: Opinion piece compares Security+ and SSCP certifications
summary: An article argues that Security+ builds foundational knowledge while ISC2's SSCP shows operational readiness. It is career and certification content with no threat information.
